newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir's party supporters quit opposition state.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir's party supporters quit opposition state.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's party members said on Sunday they had left their political posts in opposition-ruled Kelantan after failing to make headway in the northeastern Malaysian state.
Political analysts, however, interpreted the move as a ploy by Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) to seize control of the state, run by the Parti Islam Se-Malaysia (PAS).

"The opportunity given to PAS to govern Kelantan for more than 25 years is enough to show the people how weak the PAS leadership is," Rozali Isohak, spokesman for the three politicians who resigned, told Bernama news agency.
"We do not want to face questions from our supporters by continuing to stay with them," Rozali said.
The trio were part of the opposition Spirit of 46 party, which used to jointly rule Kelantan with PAS until defecting to Mahathir's UMNO this year.
Mahathir recently ordered the three Spirit politicians and another to quit the PAS-dominated Kelantan government. The fourth Spirit member died in a road accident earlier this month.
Kelantan, economically-backward but rich in oil and gas, is the only one of Malaysia's 13 states ruled by the opposition.
Political analysts said Mahathir's government was determined to recapture the state to complete its control over the country.
